Bigfoot! is out to provide a good time, through means sillier than you thought possible.
What the world needs now is a mirthful diversion and Bigfoot! is it.
Bigfoot! doesn’t stamp a big enough footprint on the heart.
Ruffin’s fingerprints are all over the musical’s barrage of punchy one-liners, but much like the mayor’s ploy, it’s not enough to distract from the overall flimsiness.
They do a fine job with parts that are just not as good as their best material.

Although the show unfortunately tends to be performed with a slyly aren’t-we-being-funny attitude that can be annoying, especially when the material proves to be not always so brilliant, Bigfoot! offers at least a pleasant waste of time.
These one-liners are the lifeblood of the brilliance of Bigfoot! and what keeps people entranced.
Campy, over the top, and utterly ridiculous, Bigfoot! follows in the tradition of hilarious musicals like Evil Dead or Avenger.
Bigfoot! is a furry, funky love letter to misfits, packed with kooky characters, 80s synth-pop charm, and a heart bigger than its leading man's footprint.
The story’s shortcomings might matter less if the score were more memorable.
This is a high-energy, laugh-packed musical comedy that knows exactly what it's doing — and does it with an absurdly talented cast.

cn.t: Critics find this goofy musical satire about a lovable monster and corrupt politicians mostly charming, praising Grey Henson's unhinged lead performance and Amber Ruffin's sharp comedic writing, though some feel the jokes are hit-or-miss.

vr.q: It's a perfect night out with friends if you just wanna laugh for ninety straight minutes. And you'll just leave so much happier than when you walked in.
